root_cause.text: The `dump_mac_header()` function in `net/netfilter/nf_log_syslog.c` fails to verify that the MAC header is actually set (using `skb_mac_header_was_set()`) before reading it, relying solely on a comparison (`skb->mac_header != skb->network_header`) that passes even when `mac_header` contains the unset sentinel value `0xffff`, leading to an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "The fallback path of dump_mac_header() guards the MAC header access only with 'skb->mac_header != skb->network_header', without checking skb_mac_header_was_set(). When the MAC header is unset, mac_header is 0xffff, so the test passes and skb_mac_header(skb) returns skb->head + 0xffff, ~64 KiB past the buffer; the loop then reads dev->hard_header_len bytes out of bounds into the kernel log." The patch adds `skb_mac_header_was_set(skb)` and uses `skb_mac_header_len(skb) != 0` instead of the open-coded comparison.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix detection of MAC header presence by using dedicated skb helpers instead of comparing raw offsets.
intent_record.what: Changed condition in dump_mac_header() from comparing mac_header and network_header pointers to using skb_mac_header_was_set() and checking that skb_mac_header_len() is non-zero.
intent_record.how: The old condition relied on pointer equality/inequality, which could be unreliable; the new condition explicitly checks whether the MAC header has been set and has a positive length, ensuring the MAC header is only dumped when it is genuinely present.
